purpose: Gatifloxacin is an antibiotic used mainly as eye drops to treat bacterial eye infections, such as pink eye (conjunctivitis). The oral form (Tequin) was previously used for infections like pneumonia and sinus infections, but it has been withdrawn from most markets due to serious blood sugar problems. Today it is most commonly used in eye drop form.
how_it_works: Gatifloxacin works by attacking and disabling the machinery that bacteria need to copy their own DNA. Without being able to reproduce, the bacteria stop growing and eventually die off. This helps your immune system clear the infection more easily.
common_side_effects: When used as eye drops, you may notice temporary eye irritation, burning, stinging, redness, or blurry vision right after putting the drops in. These effects are usually mild and go away quickly.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to any antibiotic in the fluoroquinolone family (like ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin). The oral form of this drug was removed from many markets because it caused dangerous swings in blood sugar levels. If using the eye drops, avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any surface to keep it clean. Contact lens wearers should avoid wearing lenses while treating an eye infection.
typical_dosing: For eye drops (Zymaxid 0.5%): On day one, place one drop in the affected eye every two hours while awake, up to 8 times a day. From days two through seven, use one drop two to four times a day while awake. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions.
